paragraphs.text: A fictional classroom experiment
The aim was to compare the change in colour in two labelled sample tubes.
We recorded the colour once after ten minutes. The room temperature was not recorded.
Tube A appeared darker than tube B. This observation alone does not establish a difference in concentration.

review_focus: Distinguish an observation from a measurement; discuss the limit of one observation without inventing data.

paragraphs.text: Should a fictional university retain a quiet study room?
The university should retain one quiet room while allowing collaborative work elsewhere.
A quiet room offers a clear option for students who want to read without conversation. However, this argument does not show how many rooms are needed.
An objection is that every room should support group work. A mixed arrangement could address both purposes, although space constraints need to be considered.

review_focus: Assess the qualified thesis and objection; do not require experimental results.

paragraphs.text: Comparing two fictional studies of study spaces
This exercise compares invented Study A and Study B; neither is a real publication.
Study A used interviews about preferred spaces, whereas Study B counted visits. Their outcomes therefore describe different aspects of space use.
The difference in methods prevents a direct comparison of preference with attendance. These two examples cannot establish a gap across an entire research field.

review_focus: Recognise synthesis and limits; fictional source labels must never be presented as verified citations.

paragraphs.text: A proposed evaluation of fictional library signs
The project will ask whether readers can find a reserved shelf using a revised sign.
Volunteers will attempt a shelf-location task, after which we will ask which wording was confusing. No observations have yet been collected.
Participation will be voluntary and names will not be collected. The timetable depends on permission to use the space.

review_focus: Evaluate the proposed design and feasibility; absence of completed results is expected.

paragraphs.text: A fictional document study of library notices
This classroom exercise compared three invented notices, selected because each described a different borrowing rule.
We coded whether each notice stated a deadline and a contact route. Two included a deadline; one included a contact route.
The small constructed set illustrates a coding process. It cannot establish how real library users respond to notices.

review_focus: Review transparent document analysis; do not impose laboratory controls.

paragraphs.text: A fictional student society booking problem
The case states that two teams requested the same room and neither received a confirmation. It gives no attendance data.
The main problem may be unclear confirmation responsibility rather than excessive demand. This interpretation remains an assumption to check.
A shared booking log offers visibility but requires someone to maintain it. A designated coordinator adds accountability but may become a bottleneck.

review_focus: Assess diagnosis and tradeoffs without inventing case facts.

paragraphs.text: Reflection on an invented group exercise
I assumed everyone understood the task because no one asked a question. We later produced incompatible outlines.
I now see that silence did not establish shared understanding. I could have asked each person to explain the agreed aim before we divided the work.
At the next exercise I will record the agreed aim and ask the group to review it after the first draft.

review_focus: Accept first person and assess reflection and action; do not evaluate the writer’s personality.

paragraphs.text: 给新同学的一则虚构图书角使用说明
欢迎使用班级图书角。借书前请在登记表写下书名和借阅日期。
看完后请将书放回原来的位置。如果找不到登记表，可以先联系值日同学。
这里没有说明归还期限。请根据本班约定补充，再发给新同学。

review_focus: Review purpose, audience and clarity in Chinese; no academic references or experiment sections are required.
